races.title: State Senate, District 42
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mrs. Woodson Bradley
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented North Carolina Senate District 42 since January 1, 2025, succeeding Rachel Hunt. Her campaign site describes her as a survivor, business owner, mom, wife and advocate. She won re-election on November 3, 2026.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations. Ballotpedia also lists several Sway voting groups, including NC Public School Champions.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Woodson Bradley was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. We also found no details of her business or any earlier career or elected office. The pages we read did not show the contents of the bills she sponsored. We found no documented statements or actions from her on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site names women's rights, strong public schools, safe communities and a prosperous business climate as priorities but gives no specifics. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had.

qual.background: She has served in the North Carolina Senate since January 2025 and was re-elected in 2026. Her campaign site calls her a business owner. It gives no details of that business or any other career.
qual.why: A sitting state senator with one term of legislative service, plus a self-described business background. Her committee seats add nothing to the score. Her career details aren't documented, so the score stays below the top range.

cands.name: Stacie McGinn
cands.bio: Charlotte attorney and former Bank of America executive who oversaw the bank's global consumer legal group. Earlier a partner at Skadden, working on bank mergers and consumer protection. Republican nominee for NC Senate District 42 in 2024 and 2026. Has not held elected office.
cands.gaps: Her birthplace and birth year were not found. The exact year she moved to North Carolina was not found; her campaign site says only that she has lived in Charlotte for 21 years. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for her. She has never held elected office, so there is no voting record or official action to report. We found no stated positions on data centers, new development, land ownership by investors or foreigners, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or teacher pay. Her statement about parental rights in education is general and does not address vouchers or charters. Her claims of a co-authored op-ed and of work in the Reagan Administration are self-reported and were not independently confirmed.

local.label: Roots 40: Her campaign site says she has made Charlotte home for the last 21 years, which means she moved to North Carolina as an adult, and she grew up in a military family in the West.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lawyer for 30+ years: Skadden partner who co-founded a consumer protection regulatory investigations and enforcement group and co-authored a consumer protection law book, then a Bank of America top executive (Deputy General Counsel, Global Consumer Bank) on a team overseeing a $30 billion budget. She has not held elected office.
qual.why: Long law, regulatory and executive career with budget exposure fits the middle-to-upper range; she has no prior legislative service, and the budget and policy work is self-reported.

back-police-order.evidence: Says her campaign priorities include supporting law enforcement and keeping violent criminals and those who are a danger to themselves or others off the streets.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says she supports policies keeping personal income and property taxes low, and said a November referendum would help control rising property tax rates. She did not describe a plan to eliminate homestead taxes.
